# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Refactor: decompose `packages/shared/src/database.ts` god class

## Problem statement

`packages/shared/src/database.ts` is 3,684 lines and holds a single
`WorklogDatabase` class with 109 methods spanning at least ten unrelated
concerns (work-item CRUD, hierarchy traversal, dependency-edge reconciliation,
comment storage, audit results, FTS/semantic search, sort-index management, the
`wl next` selection pipeline, JSONL import/export, and Git/JSONL sync). It
breaches the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 and is hard to navigate, review, and change safely.

## Users

- **Agents implementing work items** — need to locate the code for one concern
  without reading 3,684 lines; large files inflate context cost and increase
  the chance of editing the wrong overload.
- **Reviewers / producers auditing changes** — need diffs scoped to one
  responsibility; a 3,684-line file makes review of a 20-line behavioural
  change impractical.
- **Operators debugging `wl next`** — need the selection pipeline (the largest
  cluster: ~1,150 lines) to be readable in isolation.

Example user stories:

- As an agent, I want `wl next` selection logic in its own module, so that a
  change to selection ordering does not require loading CRUD, sync and comment
  code into context.
- As a reviewer, I want each extracted module to have a single stated
  responsibility, so that I can judge a diff against one boundary.
- As a maintainer, I want the public `WorklogDatabase` API unchanged, so that
  no CLI/Herdr/TUI consumer needs touching.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ceiling met.** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and every file under
   `packages/shared/src/database/` is ≤ 1,000 lines (target: largest extracted
   module ≤ 700). Verified with `wc -l` output recorded in the work item.
2. **Public API unchanged.** `WorklogDatabase` (all public method signatures and
   constructor), plus `WorklogDatabaseServices`, `JsonlImportResult`,
   `GitTarget`, `UpdateIfMatchesResult` and `normalizeTitleForMatch` remain
   importable from the unchanged specifier `@worklog/shared` (entry
   `dist/database.js`). No changes to `src/**` or `packages/herdr/src/**`
   consumer code.
3. **Move-only, behaviour-preserving.** No logic, SQL, error-message, ordering,
   or schema changes; existing test assertions are unmodified and the suite is
   green. Test files may be split/moved only where a test file itself exceeds
   1,000 lines (lockstep rule), with import paths the only mechanical change.
4. **No circular imports.** The extracted-module import graph is acyclic; no
   module imports the `database.ts` façade. Shared types live in a context
   module that every extracted module may import.
5. **Responsibilities documented.** `packages/shared/README.md` (Package
   Structure) and each new module's header comment state its single
   responsibility and its boundary.
6. **No performance regression** in the `wl next` path: `npm run
   benchmark:wl-next:json` pre/post comparison within run-to-run noise (the
   extraction moves code only, and `EdgeCache`/effective-priority caching
   semantics are unchanged).
7. **Builds and tests.** `npm run build:shared`, `npm run build` and the full
   project test suite all pass.
8. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes,
   including code comments, `packages/shared/README.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`,
   `docs/dev/fts.md`, `docs/dependency-reconciliation.md` and
   `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` (each currently names
   `packages/shared/src/database.ts` as the home of a concern).

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Extraction and method relocation only; no "while we're here"
  rewrites. Method-level decomposition of the two oversized methods
  (`handleCriticalEscalation`, 324 lines; `findNextWorkItemFromItems`, 251
  lines) is allowed **only** where required to keep an extracted file under the
  ceiling, and must land as a separate commit from the pure move.
- **No public-API growth.** Private hooks needed by extracted modules are
  expressed through an internal context type, not by making `WorklogDatabase`
  members public.
- **Icons import guard (WL-0MT2GMTAZ003VKVL).** `tests/unit/icons.test.ts`
  scans every `.ts`/`.js` file with `ICONS_FILE_RE` and fails on any relative
  `icons.js`/`icons.ts` import. Extracted modules must keep using
  `@worklog/shared/icons`.
- **`src/database.ts` (93-line CLI shim) is unchanged.**
- **No new runtime dependencies.**
- **Serialize with WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU** (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`,
  2,225 lines) — same package and build; running both decompositions
  concurrently would churn `packages/shared/dist` and invite merge conflicts.
- **Escaped backticks** only in written content; Markdown otherwise.

## Existing state

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — 3,684 lines, 6 exports: the
  `WorklogDatabase` class (109 methods), `normalizeTitleForMatch`, and four
  interfaces (`JsonlImportResult`, `GitTarget`, `UpdateIfMatchesResult`,
  `WorklogDatabaseServices`).
- Entry point: `packages/shared/package.json` → `main`/`exports["."]` =
  `./dist/database.js`; `src/database.ts` (root, 93 lines) is a thin CLI
  shim wiring CLI-specific services and re-exporting the shared class.
- Consumers: ~54 files reference the class (`src/**`, `packages/herdr/src/**`,
  `tests/**`, `scripts/**`, `bench/**`), all via `@worklog/shared` or the
  shim — none import internal members.
- Tests in lockstep: `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` (834),
  `database-dedup.test.ts` (134), `dirty-tracking.test.ts` (384),
  `audit-fingerprint-repair.test.ts` (135) — all under 1,000; plus root
  `tests/database.test.ts` (3,651) and `tests/next-regression.test.ts`
  (2,112), which exceed the ceiling and are therefore in scope for
  lockstep splitting.
- **Prior attempt did not land.** WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO ("Decompose
  WorklogDatabase god class", completed) extracted `src/lib/edge-cache.ts` and
  `src/lib/audit-store.ts` on the feature branch only — neither file exists in
  the current tree, and the class has since grown from 2,584 to 3,684 lines.
  This item therefore restarts from a single-class module, and the regrowth is
  the reason the decomposition needs a clear ownership boundary rather than
  ad-hoc extraction.

## Desired change

Extract cohesive modules under `packages/shared/src/database/`, leaving
`database.ts` as a façade that constructs the collaborators and delegates.
Proposed map (method attribution is exhaustive; every current method belongs to
exactly one row):

| Module | Responsibility | Est. lines |
|---|---|---|
| `database.ts` (façade) | Construction/service wiring, delegation, `close()`, existing barrel re-exports | ~400 |
| `database/context.ts` | Shared internal types (`EdgeCache`, database context/hooks), `buildChildrenByParent`, `laterTimestamp`, id generation and prefix accessors, `normalizeTitleForMatch` | ~290 |
| `database/work-items.ts` | Item CRUD (`create`, `createWithNextSortIndex`, `get`, `update`, `updateIfMatches`, `delete`, `list`, duplicate detection, diff helpers) | ~470 |
| `database/hierarchy.ts` | Children/descendants/depth/leaf queries, `cascadePriorityDowngrade`, `demoteParentOnChildAdded`, `revertToPlanComplete` | ~200 |
| `database/dependencies.ts` | Edge CRUD, `buildEdgeCache`, blocker queries, dependency-status reconciliation | ~260 |
| `database/comments.ts` | Comment CRUD, `upsertComments`/`importComments`, activity stamping | ~180 |
| `database/audit.ts` | Audit-result CRUD, waiver set/clear, invalidation reconcile, audit map + not-ready freshness | ~130 |
| `database/sort.ts` | `sortItemsByScore`, sort-index compute/assign/preview, `reSort`, `orderBySortIndex`, audit-tier comparison, `selectBySortIndex` | ~310 |
| `database/priority.ts` | `getPriorityValue`, `riskOrdinal`, `effortOrdinal`, `matchesRiskEffort`, `computeEffectivePriority` | ~200 |
| `database/next-pipeline.ts` | `findNextWorkItem`/`findNextWorkItems`/`findNextWorkItemFromItems`, `applyFilters`, `filterCandidates`, `resolveBlockerToRoot`, `selectHighestPriorityBlocking` | ~600 |
| `database/critical-escalation.ts` | `handleCriticalEscalation` and its private helpers (may require an internal split to stay under budget) | ~330 |
| `database/search.ts` | `search`, `rebuildFtsIndex`, semantic-index create/trigger/remove | ~210 |
| `database/sync.ts` | `refreshFromGit`, `exportForSync`, export timestamps, `countDirtyRecords`, delta metadata, `deleteLocalJsonl`, `refreshFromJsonlIfNewer`, auto-sync triggers | ~380 |
| `database/import-export.ts` | `import`, `upsertItems`, `clear`, `getAll*` snapshots | ~200 |

Dependency direction after extraction:
`database.ts` → {any module}; modules → `context.ts` + `../types.js` +
`../persistent-store.js` + `@worklog/shared/icons`. No module → `database.ts`.

### Proposed child decomposition (structural slices)

1. **Foundation** — create `database/` and `database/context.ts` (internal
   types, EdgeCache, children map, id generation, prefix accessors). Blocks the
   rest.
2. **`wl next` cluster** — `priority.ts`, `next-pipeline.ts`,
   `critical-escalation.ts` (largest win, highest risk).
3. **Ordering & audit** — `sort.ts`, `audit.ts`.
4. **Items & hierarchy** — `work-items.ts`, `hierarchy.ts`.
5. **Dependencies & comments** — `dependencies.ts`, `comments.ts`.
6. **Search, sync & import/export + closeout** — `search.ts`, `sync.ts`,
   `import-export.ts`, oversized test-file splits, docs/README, final `wc -l`
   evidence, build and full suite.

Slices are ordered so that slice 1 blocks the rest; each slice is move-only and
independently verifiable.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — façade after extraction; public API must
  stay byte-compatible at the type level
- `packages/shared/src/database/*.ts` — new cohesive modules (map above)
- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts`, `database-dedup.test.ts`,
  `dirty-tracking.test.ts`, `audit-fingerprint-repair.test.ts` — imports stay
  `./database.js`; assertions unchanged
- `tests/database.test.ts` (3,651) — split in lockstep, move-only
- `tests/next-regression.test.ts` (2,112) — split in lockstep, move-only
- `packages/shared/README.md` — Package Structure section
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/dev/fts.md`,
  `docs/dependency-reconciliation.md`, `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` —
  update file references to the new module paths
- `bench/wl-next-perf.ts` — pre/post performance evidence (no change expected)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Behaviour drift in the `wl next` pipeline** (largest, most intricate
  cluster; 324- and 251-line methods). *Mitigation:* pure move first; split
  oversized methods in separate commits; `tests/next-regression.test.ts`
  and `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md` act as the behaviour oracle.
- **Circular imports** (`next-pipeline` ↔ `dependencies` ↔ `priority`).
  *Mitigation:* `context.ts` owns shared types; modules receive collaborators
  through the context; façade is never imported by a module.
- **Hidden `this.` coupling.** Several "private" helpers are shared across
  concerns (`buildEdgeCache`, `generateId`, `buildAuditMapForItems`,
  `compareTrackedFields`, `getPriorityValue`, `getNonClosedChildren`,
  `debug`). *Mitigation:* inventory every `this.` call per method before the
  move and express it on the context type.
- **Build/packaging regression.** `packages/shared` `main`/`exports` point at
  `dist/database.js`; the façade must keep that path and re-export every type.
- **Performance regression** through changed cache lifetimes. *Mitigation:*
  `npm run benchmark:wl-next:json` before and after the `wl next` cluster.
- **Regrowth repeats** (this file grew 2,584 → 3,684 after a "completed"
  decomposition). *Mitigation within scope:* documented module boundaries and
  single-responsibility headers. A repo-wide file-size guard is **out of
  scope** here and filed separately (see Related work) to avoid scope creep.
- **Merge contention** with WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`).
  *Mitigation:* serialise the two items; do not run both concurrently.
- **Assumption:** the 1,000-line ceiling applies to non-test source, and to
  test files only when they are touched in lockstep with their module.
- **Assumption:** no consumer call-site changes are acceptable, including in
  `scripts/` and `bench/`.
- **Assumption:** no behavioural improvement is bundled in; any improvement
  observed en route becomes a separate `discovered-from` work item.

## Related work

- WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — parent sweep: every production file > 1,000 lines is
  evaluated for decomposition (producer directive, Q1 answered).
- WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO — prior "Decompose WorklogDatabase god class"
  (completed, but the extracted `src/lib/edge-cache.ts` /
  `src/lib/audit-store.ts` never landed on `main`; informs the
  `context.ts` + `audit.ts` boundaries proposed here).
- WL-0MQPQOFVX003V32B — Phase 1: extracted `WorklogDatabase` into
  `packages/shared/` (explains the `src/database.ts` shim split).
- WL-0MV85WFYU0071YQ9 — removed `needsProducerReview` from the worklog core
  (recent material change inside this file).
- WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU — sibling: decompose
  `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` (same package; serialise).
- WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B, WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6, WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ — companion
  god-class items from the same sweep.
- Repo docs that name this file as a home of a concern: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
  (§ sort ordering, § database init), `docs/dev/fts.md` (`search()`),
  `docs/dependency-reconciliation.md` (§ reconciliation logic),
  `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` (`exportForSync()`),
  `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md`
  (`findNextWorkItemFromItems`).
- Discovered during intake: repo-wide file-size guard (created separately,
  `discovered-from:WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT`).

## Appendix: decision log (agent-proposed; producer may override)

No producer interview questions were required: the seed context (goal, drafted
ACs, parent directive) is sufficient to draft an actionable brief, and every
remaining choice is a reversible design decision that the plan/implement stages
can adjust. The three decisions below were taken by the agent and are recorded
for review.

- **Q: How should extracted modules relate to `WorklogDatabase`?**
  **Recommended and chosen: (a)** pure functional modules operating on an
  injected internal context type, with `WorklogDatabase` as a delegating
  façade. Rationale: testable without a database, no inheritance/mixin
  complexity, and the import graph stays acyclic (the façade depends on the
  modules, never the reverse).
  Alternatives considered: (b) composed private helper classes instantiated by
  the façade (more state plumbing, harder to test in isolation); (c) mixins /
  `extends` chains (fragile, obscures the public surface).

- **Q: What child granularity?**
  **Recommended and chosen:** six children (foundation; `wl next` cluster;
  ordering & audit; items & hierarchy; dependencies & comments; search, sync &
  import/export + closeout). Rationale: each child is independently move-only,
  verifiable with the full suite, and small enough to review; the riskiest
  cluster (`wl next`) is isolated so a regression is bisectable.
  Alternatives considered: ~13 children (one per module — more overhead and
  churn than value); one child (no bisectable checkpoints).

- **Q: Add a file-size regression guard (CI/lint) in this item?**
  **Recommended and chosen: no — out of scope.** A guard is repo-wide policy
  affecting every sibling god-class item, not a property of this file.
  Filed as a separate low-priority `chore` item (`discovered-from` this item).

- **Q: Should the oversized test files (`tests/database.test.ts` 3,651;
  `tests/next-regression.test.ts` 2,112) be split?**
  **Recommended and chosen: yes, mechanical split only**, in lockstep with the
  module extraction, because the parent sweep rule evaluates test files in
  lockstep with their module. Assertions, `describe` titles and fixture
  helpers are unchanged; only file location/imports move.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQPQOFVX003V32B** – Phase 1 — Extract WorklogDatabase into packages/shared/ (completed)
- **WL-0MTFNIXM3000NFVC** – Attribute real deletes: shared delete + CLI/API wiring (completed)
- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** – Remove packages/herdr/src/icons.ts and rewire herdr consumers (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptable, acceptance, act, actionable, activity (+359 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: act, activity, add, ade, adopted (+337 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: act, actionable, activity, add, ade (+325 more)

# Refactor: decompose `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` god class

## Problem statement

`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` is 2,340 lines and holds a single
`SqlitePersistentStore` class spanning at least eight unrelated concerns
(connection open/read-only handling, schema DDL and additive repair, metadata
and delta-sync watermarks, work-item CRUD with hierarchy ordering, comment
CRUD, dependency-edge CRUD, audit-result CRUD, FTS5 index/search, and an
in-memory query cache). It breaches the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling
adopted for WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 and is hard to navigate, review and change
safely.

## Users

- **Agents implementing work items** — need to locate one concern (e.g. the FTS
  search path) without loading 2,340 unrelated lines into context.
- **Reviewers / producers auditing changes** — need a diff whose blast radius
  is legible from the touched module.
- **Operators / maintainers debugging storage behaviour** — need the read-only
  open contract, cache invalidation rules and FTS fallback readable in
  isolation.

Example user stories:

- As an agent, I want the FTS search/fallback logic in its own module, so that
  a change to ranking does not require reading schema, audit and comment code.
- As a reviewer, I want each extracted module to declare a single
  responsibility, so that I can judge a diff against one boundary.
- As a maintainer, I want `SqlitePersistentStore`'s public surface unchanged, so
  that `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and the benchmark consumers need no
  edits.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ceiling met.** `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` and every file
   under `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/` is ≤ 1,000 lines (target:
   largest extracted module ≤ 600). Verified with pre/post `wc -l` output
   recorded on the work item.
2. **Public surface preserved.** `SqlitePersistentStore`,
   `PersistentStoreServices`, `PersistentStoreCacheOptions`,
   `PersistentStoreOpenOptions`, `FtsSearchResult`, `LastExportTimestamps`,
   `MigrationInfo`, `normalizeSqliteValue`, `normalizeSqliteBindings`,
   `unescapeText` and `parseAuditWaiver` remain importable from the unchanged
   specifiers `./persistent-store.js` (package build `dist/persistent-store.js`)
   with identical types and behaviour. Consumers —
   `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and `scripts/benchmark-caching.ts` — need
   no import-path edits.
3. **Move-only, behaviour-preserving.** No logic, SQL, ordering, error-message,
   schema, cache-semantics or public-signature change. No existing test file is
   modified (import paths, fixtures or assertions); all
   `packages/shared/src/*.test.ts` suites and the full project suite pass
   unchanged.
4. **No circular imports.** The extracted-module import graph is acyclic; no
   module imports the `persistent-store.ts` façade. Shared internal state
   (`db` handle, cache, SQL-binding helpers, row mappers) is reached through an
   internal context type, not by modules importing the façade.
5. **Responsibilities documented.** Each new module carries a header comment
   stating its single responsibility; `packages/shared/README.md` (Package
   Structure) lists the new layout.
6. **Builds and tests.** `npm run build:shared`, `npm run build` and the full
   project test suite pass (run through the test skill, not ad-hoc commands).
7. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes,
   including code comments, `packages/shared/README.md`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`,
   `docs/design/incremental-sync.md`, `docs/dev/sync-persist-performance.md` and
   `docs/dev/wal-checkpointing-investigation.md` where they name this file as the
   home of a concern.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Extraction and relocation only; no "while we're here"
  rewrites. Method-level decomposition of any oversized method is allowed only
  where required to keep an extracted file under the ceiling, and lands as a
  separate commit from the pure move.
- **Barrel compatibility.** `persistent-store.ts` stays as the public entry,
  re-exporting the full current export set (11 symbols). It is not in the
  package `exports` map, but `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and
  `scripts/benchmark-caching.ts` (`dist/persistent-store.js`) resolve it by
  path, so the file must remain.
- **Package layout.** New modules live under
  `packages/shared/src/persistent-store/`, mirroring the `src/database/`
  layout agreed for the sibling epic WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT. `tsconfig` already
  includes `src/**/*`, so no build-config change is required.
- **Serialise with WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT** (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`) —
  same package and build; running both decompositions concurrently would churn
  `packages/shared/dist` and invite merge conflicts. Do not run both at once.
- **Scope boundary.** Only `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`. The root
  sibling `src/persistent-store.ts` (1,653 lines) has its own item
  (WL-0MVGKGU19004NTHB) and is **out of scope**; the two files are divergent
  forks (the shared copy adds read-only open, audit-waiver parsing, the query
  cache and delta-sync watermarks), so no cross-file unification is attempted
  here.
- **No new runtime dependencies.** No changes to the wl CLI contract, storage
  schema, or the `@worklog/shared` package `exports` map.
- **Escaped backticks** only in written content; Markdown otherwise.

## Existing state

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — 2,340 lines, 11 exports.
- Consumers (all resolve the same barrel path): `packages/shared/src/database.ts`
  imports `SqlitePersistentStore`, `FtsSearchResult`,
  `PersistentStoreServices`, `PersistentStoreCacheOptions`,
  `LastExportTimestamps`, `unescapeText`;
  `scripts/benchmark-caching.ts` dynamically imports
  `dist/persistent-store.js` for `SqlitePersistentStore`. No other source file
  imports the module directly.
- In-lockstep tests: `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` (839),
  `dirty-tracking.test.ts` (384), `database-dedup.test.ts` (134),
  `audit-fingerprint-repair.test.ts` (135), `database-readonly.test.ts` (185)
  — all under 1,000 and exercise `SqlitePersistentStore` through
  `WorklogDatabase`. No test file needs splitting.
- Current section inventory (from the `dev` checkout):

| Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Module doc, interfaces, SQL-binding/waiver utilities | 1–258 | 258 |
| Constructor, connection open, read-only handling, schema init/repair | 259–594 | 336 |
| Metadata, last-export timestamps, delta-sync metadata | 595–705 | 111 |
| Work-item CRUD, sort-index and hierarchy ordering | 706–1186 | 481 |
| Comment CRUD | 1187–1287 | 101 |
| Dependency edges, `importData`, transactions | 1288–1449 | 162 |

## Refactor: decompose `src/sync.ts` god class

**File:** `src/sync.ts` (1,867 lines, 34 exports)

## Problem statement

`src/sync.ts` exceeds the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (downtime-worker.ts decomposition). It concentrates
merge logic, author-identity validation, remote fetching, delta replay and
push operations in a single module, making navigation, review and safe
change harder than necessary.

## Users

- **Developer maintaining sync** — needs to locate and edit one concern without
  scrolling 1,800 lines. *As a maintainer, I want merge logic isolated from git
  plumbing so a merge fix does not require reading push code.*
- **Code reviewer** — needs a focused diff surface per concern.
  *As a reviewer, I want to review a change confined to one cohesive file.*
- **New contributor** — needs learnable module sizes.
  *As a newcomer, I want each sync concern to be a file I can read in one sitting.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** Every file in the resulting structure
   (barrel and extracted modules) has ≤ 1,000 lines, verified mechanically
   (e.g. `wc -l`) and recorded in the completion comment.
2. **Public API surface preserved.** All 34 existing exports remain importable
   from `'../src/sync.js'` / `'./sync.js'` (barrel re-export); no consumer
   source file or test file changes its import path or assertions.
   Verified by `tsc` build plus an unchanged test suite.
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only.** No logic changes; existing tests pass
   without modification. Any accidental behavioural delta must be reverted,
   not "fixed" in place.
4. **No new circular imports.** Dependency direction is acyclic and recorded in
   the module responsibility table below; verified by build plus an import-graph
   check (no module imports a module that imports it back).
5. **Module responsibilities documented.** Each extracted file carries a
   top-level JSDoc comment naming its concern.
6. **Validation.** Full project test suite passes via the test skill, and
   `npm run build` succeeds.
7. **Documentation updated.** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (or the sync section it
   links) describes the new module layout; code comments reflect moved code.

## Constraints

- Preserve the public API exactly — barrel re-export only, no consumer edits.
- No new dependencies, no behavioural changes, no renames of exported symbols.
- Follow the existing `src/sync/` sub-module pattern (`merge-utils.ts` already
  lives there) and the `sync-defaults.ts` / `sync-phase-timings.ts` precedent.
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` imports `MergeOptions` from `'../sync.js'`; it may
  be re-pointed to the new types module (internal, not a consumer).
- Scope is decomposition only. Any behavioural improvement discovered is filed
  as a separate work item, not absorbed here.

## Existing state

- `src/sync.ts` — 1,867 lines, 34 exports (23 functions/consts + 11
  interfaces/types), no internal section markers; concerns are inferable from
  declaration order.
- Already extracted: `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` (52 lines, merge primitives),
  `src/sync-defaults.ts`, `src/sync-phase-timings.ts`.
- 10 source files import from `sync.js`: `database.ts`, `github-sync.ts`,
  `api.ts`, `logging.ts`, `index.ts`, `commands/{sync,doctor,init,migrate,helpers}.ts`.
- 11 test files import from `sync.js` (`sync.test.ts`, `sync-whitelist.test.ts`,
  `sync-author-gate.test.ts`, `sync-worktree.test.ts`,
  `rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts`, `sync-regression-guard.test.ts`,
  `sync-prefix-filter.test.ts`, `config-sync-allowed-authors.test.ts`, and others).
- Recent history touching the file: `f39b2463` (sync phase timings),
  `4eb0cc6b` (claim-hold guard), `09ac2db7` (audit downgrade guard) — the file
  is under active change, which raises merge-conflict risk during the refactor.

## Desired change — module plan (cycle-safe)

Extract along the existing cohesive concern groups; `src/sync.ts` becomes a thin
barrel. Est. line counts derive from the current file's declaration ranges.

| New file | Est. lines | Contents | Depends on |
|----------|-----------|----------|------------|
| `src/sync.ts` (barrel) | ~60 | Re-exports of every module below | all |
| `src/sync/types.ts` | ~100 | `GitTarget`, `SyncResult`, `MergeOptions`, `IncomingCommit`, `SyncAllowedAuthors`, `AuthorIdentityOptions`, `AuthorIdentityViolation`, `AuthorIdentityResult`, `DeltaReplayResult` | `../types.js` |
| `src/sync/git-exec.ts` | ~90 | `sanitizeGitEnv`, `gitExecAsync`, `execAsync`, `execGitCaptureStdout`, `escapeShellArg` | `../process-lifecycle.js` |
| `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts` | ~80 | `isRegressionDefault`, `isValueRegression`, `isEmptyMeaningfulField`, `isTerminalStage`, `isAttributedDelete` | `types.ts`, `merge-utils.ts` |
| `src/sync/field-merge.ts` | ~600 | `mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `mergeRemoteItem`, `indexItemsById` | `merge-predicates.ts`, `merge-utils.ts`, `types.ts` |
| `src/sync/merge.ts` | ~30 | `mergeWorkItems` | `field-merge.ts`, `types.ts` |
| `src/sync/merge-collateral.ts` | ~130 | `mergeComments`, `mergeAuditResults`, `mergeDependencyEdges` | `merge-utils.ts`, `types.ts` |
| `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` | ~70 | `isOwnProjectItemId`, `filterRemoteDataByPrefix` | `types.ts` |
| `src/sync/author-identity.ts` | ~200 | `normalizeEmail`, `isAllowAllAuthors`, `isEmailWhitelisted`, `getRemoteAuthorCommits`, `checkAuthorIdentity`, `buildIdentityRefusalMessage`, `getConfiguredUserEmail`, `enforceAuthorIdentityGate` | `git-exec.ts`, `types.ts` |
| `src/sync/refs.ts` | ~110 | `getLastSyncedRefPath`, `readLastSyncedRef`, `writeLastSyncedRef`, `getRemoteTrackingRefSha`, `getRemoteTrackingRef`, `_testOnly_getRemoteTrackingRef` | `git-exec.ts` |
| `src/sync/repo-context.ts` | ~60 | `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, `getRepoRelativePath` | `git-exec.ts` |
| `src/sync/worktree.ts` | ~140 | `removeWorktreeFiles`, `listTrackedFiles`, `ensureDir`, `withTempWorktree` | `git-exec.ts`, `types.ts` |
| `src/sync/remote.ts` | ~200 | `getRemoteDataFileContentWithRef`, `getRemoteDataFileContent`, `replayRemoteDeltaChain` | `worktree.ts`, `git-exec.ts`, `refs.ts`, `repo-context.ts`, `../jsonl.js` |
| `src/sync/push.ts` | ~170 | `gitPushDataFileToBranch`, `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` | `worktree.ts`, `remote.ts`, `git-exec.ts`, `repo-context.ts` |

The layering is strictly bottom-up (`types`/`git-exec` → predicates → merge →
remote/worktree → push → barrel), so no cycle is created. Note that
`mergeRemoteItem` must live in `field-merge.ts` (not `merge.ts`) to avoid a
`merge → field-merge → merge` cycle.

## Key Files

- `src/sync.ts` — Reduced to a barrel re-export preserving all 34 exports.
- `src/sync/types.ts` — Shared sync types currently interleaved with logic.
- `src/sync/git-exec.ts` — Git invocation, env sanitisation, stdout capture.
- `src/sync/merge-predicates.ts` — "is this a regression / a default" predicates.
- `src/sync/field-merge.ts` — Same- and different-timestamp field merge (largest extract).
- `src/sync/merge.ts` — Public merge entry point.
- `src/sync/merge-collateral.ts` — Comment, audit-result and dependency-edge merge.
- `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` — Cross-project prefix filtering.
- `src/sync/author-identity.ts` — Author identity gate and whitelist logic.
- `src/sync/refs.ts` — Last-synced ref and remote-tracking ref helpers.
- `src/sync/repo-context.ts` — Data-file/repo-root resolution and assertion.
- `src/sync/worktree.ts` — Temporary worktree lifecycle helpers.
- `src/sync/remote.ts` — Remote content fetch and delta-replay chain.
- `src/sync/push.ts` — Data-file push and force-push/rewrite.
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — Existing primitives; re-point `MergeOptions` import.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — Document the new sync module layout.

## Risks & Assumptions

**Risks**
- **Merge-logic interdependence** — `mergeSameTimestampItems` /
  `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` interlock with `mergeRemoteItem`; hence the
  explicit placement of `mergeRemoteItem` in `field-merge.ts`. Mitigation: keep
  the predicates in their own leaf module.
- **Test-coupling blast radius** — 11 test files import from `sync.js`; a
  single missing barrel re-export breaks them. Mitigation: mechanical export
  parity check (compare the exported symbol list before/after).
- **Concurrent-change conflicts** — `src/sync.ts` changed in the last three
  sync-related commits; a long-lived branch will conflict. Mitigation: land as
  a small number of sequential commits (types/git-exec first, then merge, then
  remote/push, then barrel), each building green.
- **Circular imports** — mitigated by the layered plan above and verified by
  build + import-graph check.
- **Scope creep** — the file contains known awkwardness (e.g. duplicated
  worktree/push preamble). Record opportunities as new work items; do not
  refactor logic here.
- **`_testOnly_getRemoteTrackingRef`** — a test-only export must survive the
  barrel unchanged; `tests/sync.test.ts` depends on it.

**Assumptions**
- Barrel re-export from `src/sync.ts` is the accepted compatibility mechanism
  (matches AC 2 in the seed brief and the existing `index.ts` pattern).
- Test files need no decomposition; only production source moves.
- Line targets are estimates; distribution may shift between
  `field-merge.ts` and `merge.ts` provided all files stay ≤ 1,000 lines.
- No performance or runtime-import-order change is expected.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7** — downtime-worker.ts is a god class (parent refactor
  series; this item is `discovered-from` it).
- **WL-0MSGAEJQA005QG3W** — Sync invalidation and cross-instance heartbeat
  (completed; prior work in this module).
- **WL-0MV85WBZ2004VDUQ** — Assignee sync regression guard (completed; owner of
  the `isRegressionDefault` / `isEmptyMeaningfulField` semantics that move here).
- **WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS** — Sync must not re-timestamp audit-fresh items
  (completed; touched merge paths).
- **WL-0MVGKH9Z900178UF** — decompose `src/github-sync.ts` (sibling decomposition).
- **WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ** — decompose `src/commands/init.ts` (sibling decomposition).
- **WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1** — decompose `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (sibling decomposition).

## Related docs

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — SQLite/JSONL sync architecture; needs the new module map.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — sync behaviour reference (link target for the layout).
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — relevant to `src/sync/worktree.ts` extraction.

## Appendix

- Q: How should the decomposition be structured? — Answer (repo analysis):
  Extract along the existing declaration-order concern groups into a layered,
  cycle-safe module set with a barrel re-export from `src/sync.ts`. Research:
  read all 1,867 lines' declaration ranges, the 11 test importers and 10 source
  importers; found no existing sync split beyond `merge-utils.ts`. Precedent:

- Q: Do test files need to change? — Answer (repo analysis): No. All 11 test

- As a maintainer, I want to find the `gh` CLI transport code without scanning a

2. **Unchanged public API.** `src/github.ts` re-exports exactly the same public
   names as today (the 58 exports listed in `Existing state` — no additions, no
   removals, no renames), so all consumers importing from
   `./github.js` / `../src/github.js` compile unchanged. Verified by a new
   structure test comparing the barrel's export surface against the
   pre-refactor list.
3. **Move-only, test-preserving.** No existing test file is modified (no import
   path or assertion changes) and the full existing GitHub test suite passes
   via the test skill. Existing `vi.mock('../src/github.js')` factories
   (full-replacement and `importOriginal` styles) keep working.
4. **No new circular imports.** No extracted module imports from
   `./github.js` (barrel); dependency direction is strictly
   `github.ts` → submodules → (github-types.ts, github-transport.ts), with the
   optional `github-throttler.js` consumers unchanged. Verified by a structure
   test (module-graph check) and by the TypeScript build.

   header per module + a "GitHub module layout" note in
   `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`); references to code locations updated in
   `docs/github-throttling.md` and `docs/SHELL_ESCAPING.md`; the full project
   test suite passes.

## Constraints

- All consumers keep importing from `src/github.ts` — do **not** repoint any
  consumer (e.g. `github-sync.ts`, `delegate-helper.ts`, `commands/github.ts`,
  `jsonl.ts`) to submodules. Some tests replace the whole
  `../src/github.js` module with a mock factory (e.g.
  `tests/github-sync-comments.test.ts`, `tests/cli/delegate-guard-rails.test.ts`),
  so the barrel is the single import surface.
- Extracted modules may not import from the barrel (cycle guard); the shared
  `setVerboseLogger` state lives in the transport module and stays a singleton
  (ESM module instance) reachable via the barrel.
- Behaviour-preserving: no logic, signature, or export-name changes; no new
  runtime dependencies.
- New module filenames must not collide with existing
  `src/github-sync.ts`, `src/github-throttler.ts`, `src/github-metrics.ts`,
  `src/github-pre-filter.ts`, `src/lib/github-helper.ts`.
- Scope is `src/github.ts` only; sibling files over 1,000 lines
  (`src/sync.ts` 1,867, `src/persistent-store.ts` 1,653, `src/github-sync.ts`
  1,339) have their own items.

- Only source files are measured; test files are evaluated in lockstep with
  their module (per the sweep rule) but no test file should need editing here.

## Existing state

- `src/github.ts` = 1,755 lines, 58 `export` declarations:
  - Types: `GithubConfig`, `GithubIssueRecord`, `GithubIssueComment`,
    `IssueHierarchy`, `AssignGithubIssueResult`, `LabelEvent`.
  - Transport/retry: `setVerboseLogger`, `ghApiAsyncScheduled`,
    `ghApiDetailedScheduled`, `ghApiJsonScheduled`, `isSecondaryRateLimitText`,
    `SecondaryRateLimitError` (private helpers: `runGh*`, `spawnCommand`,
    backoff/jitter).
  - Labels: `isSingleValueCategoryLabel`, `normalizeGithubLabelPrefix`,
    `ensureGithubLabelsAsync`, `LabelEventCache`, `fetchLabelEventsAsync`,
    `labelFieldsDiffer`, `getLatestLabelEventTimestamp`.
  - Utilities/markers: `parseRepoSlug`, `getRepoFromGitRemote`,
    `buildWorklogMarker`, `buildWorklogCommentMarker`, `stripWorklogMarkers`,
    `extractWorklogId`, `extractWorklogCommentId`, `extractParentId`,
    `extractParentIssueNumber`, `extractChildIds`, `extractChildIssueNumbers`.
  - Hierarchy: `getIssueHierarchy`, `getIssueHierarchyAsync`,
    `getIssueNodeIdAsync`, `addSubIssueLink`, `addSubIssueLinkResult`,
    `addSubIssueLinkResultAsync`, `listParentIssueNumbersFromTimeline`.
  - Issues/payload: `workItemToIssuePayload`, `issueToWorkItemFields`,
    `createGithubIssue`, `createGithubIssueAsync`, `updateGithubIssue`,
    `updateGithubIssueAsync`, `getGithubIssue`, `getGithubIssueAsync`,
    `listGithubIssues`, `listGithubIssuesAsync`.
  - Comments: `listGithubIssueComments`, `listGithubIssueCommentsAsync`,
    `createGithubIssueComment`, `createGithubIssueCommentAsync`,
    `updateGithubIssueComment`, `updateGithubIssueCommentAsync`,
    `getGithubIssueComment`, `getGithubIssueCommentAsync`.
  - Assignment: `assignGithubIssue`, `assignGithubIssueAsync`.
- Consumers (import from `./github.js`): `src/github-sync.ts` (30 symbols),
  `src/delegate-helper.ts` (type + lazy `assignGithubIssueAsync`),
  `src/jsonl.ts` (`stripWorklogMarkers`), `src/commands/github.ts`,
  plus 20+ test files importing from `../src/github.js` / `../../src/github.js`
  (some with full-module `vi.mock` factories).
- Prior related item WL-0MQJK4UGN000CHUF ("Split src/github.ts into
  domain-specific modules", status completed) proposed the same seams
  (`src/lib/github-issues|comments|labels|hierarchy|utils|assign.ts`), but **no
  corresponding extracted modules exist at HEAD** (commit `8e37880` is not in
  this repo's history) — treat this as a fresh decomposition; reuse the
  validated seams, and note the discrepancy in the implementation report.

## Desired change

Flat, prefixed submodules under `src/` (matches the existing
`github-sync.ts` / `github-throttler.ts` naming convention), with
`src/github.ts` reduced to a thin barrel:

| Module (new) | Contents | Est. lines |
|---|---|---|
| `src/github-types.ts` | `GithubConfig`, `GithubIssueRecord`, `GithubIssueComment`, `IssueHierarchy`, `AssignGithubIssueResult`, `LabelEvent` | ≈ 40 |
| `src/github-transport.ts` | `setVerboseLogger`, `ghApi*Scheduled`, `isSecondaryRateLimitText`, `SecondaryRateLimitError`, private `runGh*`/`spawnCommand`/backoff (incl. temp-file pagination handling) | ≈ 450 |
| `src/github-labels.ts` | `normalizeGithubLabelPrefix`, `isSingleValueCategoryLabel`, private `labelColor`/`isStatusLabel`/label caches, `ensureGithubLabelsAsync` (and private sync/deprecated variant), `LabelEventCache`, `fetchLabelEventsAsync`, `labelFieldsDiffer`, `getLatestLabelEventTimestamp` | ≈ 330 |
| `src/github-markers.ts` | `buildWorklogMarker`, `buildWorklogCommentMarker`, `stripWorklogMarkers`, `extractWorklogId`, `extractWorklogCommentId`, `extractParentId`, `extractParentIssueNumber`, `extractChildIds`, `extractChildIssueNumbers`, `parseRepoSlug`, `getRepoFromGitRemote` | ≈ 100 |
| `src/github-hierarchy.ts` | `IssueHierarchy`, `getIssueHierarchy`, `getIssueHierarchyAsync`, `getIssueNodeIdAsync`, `addSubIssueLink`, `addSubIssueLinkResult`, `addSubIssueLinkResultAsync`, `listParentIssueNumbersFromTimeline` (private `getIssueNodeId`) | ≈ 250 |
| `src/github-comments.ts` | `listGithubIssueComments(Async)`, `createGithubIssueComment(Async)`, `updateGithubIssueComment(Async)`, `getGithubIssueComment(Async)`, private `normalizeGithubIssueComment` | ≈ 105 |
| `src/github-issues.ts` | `workItemToIssuePayload`, `issueToWorkItemFields`, `LEGACY_PRIORITY_MAP`, `createGithubIssue(Async)`, `updateGithubIssue(Async)`, `getGithubIssue(Async)`, `listGithubIssues(Async)`, `assignGithubIssue(Async)`, private `normalizeGithubIssue` | ≈ 470 |
| `src/github.ts` (rewritten) | Barrel: explicit re-exports of all 58 public names from the modules above (no logic) | ≈ 120 |

`github-transport.ts`; submodules never import from `github.ts`. No module
imports `github-sync.ts` / `github-throttler.ts` / `github-pre-filter.ts` /
`github-metrics.ts` (existing shared modules stay as-is).

- asserts each `src/github*.ts` module (barrel + submodules) is < 1,000 lines;
- asserts the barrel exports exactly the pre-refactor public-name list;
- asserts no `src/github-*.ts` submodule imports `github.js` (cycle guard).

## Key Files:

- `src/github.ts` — rewrite as barrel re-exporting the 58 public names (largest
  reduction for the ceiling AC).
- `src/github-transport.ts` — move gh CLI transport/retry/backoff + verbose
  logger (new; largest extracted module ≈ 450 lines).

- `src/github-comments.ts` — move comment CRUD (new).
- `src/github-issues.ts` — move issue CRUD, payload mapping, assignment (new;
  largest module ≈ 470 lines).
- `src/github-types.ts` — move shared GitHub types (new).
- `tests/unit/github-module-structure.test.ts` — new structural regression test.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — add "GitHub module layout" subsection.
- `docs/github-throttling.md`, `docs/SHELL_ESCAPING.md` — update code-location
  references (`src/github.ts` → transport module).

## Related work

- WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — downtime-worker.ts is a god class (parent series;
  discovered-from). Source of the 1,000-line directive.
- WL-0MQJK4UGN000CHUF — Split src/github.ts into domain-specific modules
  (completed; proposed the same seams; not present at HEAD — see Existing
  state).
- WL-0MVGKH9Z900178UF — Refactor: decompose src/github-sync.ts god class
  (open; sibling — github-sync.ts imports 30 symbols from the barrel, so this
  split must keep them importable).
- WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL — Add a file-size guard so god classes cannot regrow past
  1,000 lines (open; this item's structural test is module-scoped, the guard
  item provides the global enforcement).
- WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E — Refactor guard: downtime-worker split invariants
  (in_review; precedent for the test-first invariant-gate pattern).
- WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ, WL-0MVGKGU19004NTHB — sibling decompose items for
  `src/sync.ts` / `src/persistent-store.ts` (share the barrel + unmodified-tests
  pattern; do not overlap in scope).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Mock-boundary risk (high):** tests fully replace `../src/github.js` with a
  mock factory; any consumer repointed to a submodule silently bypasses the
  mock and breaks tests. Mitigation: barrel is the only import surface; AC3
  verifies.
- **Export drift risk (medium):** 58 public names — a missed/misnamed
  re-export breaks compilation of consumers or tests. Mitigation: structure
  test pins the exact name list; `tsc` build gate.
- **Singleton state risk (low):** `setVerboseLogger` moves to the transport
  module; the ESM singleton keeps CLI `--verbose` behaviour identical — verify
  with `tests/cli/gh-api-scheduled.test.ts` and verbose-logging tests.
- **Blame/churn:** move-only commits preserve history poorly by nature; use
  `git diff --stat` per module and keep the move mechanical.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not fix or refactor logic while moving (e.g.
  deprecated `ensureGithubLabels` stays deprecated and private); record any
  improvement opportunity as a new work item, not scope.
- **Failure mode:** a barrel that re-exports a name twice (or a module that
  exports the same name as another) yields ambiguous `export *` errors — use
  explicit named re-exports in `src/github.ts`, not `export *`.
- **Estimate caveat:** module line estimates (sum ≈ 1,865) exceed today's 1,755
  because each module regains its own imports/header; the ceiling check is
  per-file, not on the total.
- **Assumption:** flat `src/github-*.ts` naming is acceptable (repo
  convention); alternative `src/lib/github-*.ts` (prior item's naming) equally
  valid — confirm choice with plan skill during planning.
- **Assumption:** the 1,000-line ceiling applies per source file; test files
  are only evaluated in lockstep and none should need edits here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview was required — the item is a move-only refactoring
`task` with explicit draft ACs, and every design question below was answered
from repo evidence. This section is the auditable record.

- Q: Are the prior split's extracted modules reusable? — Answer (agent
  research): No — `git log` confirms no `src/lib/github-*.ts` files exist at
  HEAD and commit `8e37880` (cited by WL-0MQJK4UGN000CHUF) is absent from this
  repo's history; the prior completion claim does not match the tree. The
  seams it proposed remain valid and are reused. Source: `git log --all`,
  `ls src/lib/`.
- Q: Where should extracted modules live? — Answer (agent research,
  assumption to confirm at plan): flat `src/github-<area>.ts` to match the
  existing `github-sync.ts`/`github-throttler.ts` convention and to keep
  `src/github.ts` unambiguous as the barrel. Source: `ls src/`.
- Q: Can consumers be repointed to submodules for cleanliness? — Answer
  (agent research): No — `vi.mock('../src/github.js')` full-replacement
  factories in `tests/github-sync-comments.test.ts` and
  `tests/cli/delegate-guard-rails.test.ts` require the barrel to remain the
  single import surface; AC2/AC3 encode this. Source: test files cited.
- Q: Is there an existing regression guard to reuse? — Answer (agent
  research): Partially — WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E established the test-first
  invariant-gate pattern for downtime-worker, and WL-0MVHLMKD60068VJL (open)
  will add a global >1,000-line file guard; neither exists at HEAD yet, so
  this item adds its own module-scoped structure test. Source: `wl search`,
  `wl show` of both items.
- Q: Do helper functions used only internally need to stay private? — Answer
  (agent research): Yes — private helpers (`runGh*`, `labelColor`,
  `normalizeGithubIssueComment`, deprecated `ensureGithubLabels`, etc.) move
  into their new modules but are not re-exported from the barrel, keeping the
  58-name public surface identical. Source: `grep -n "^export" src/github.ts`.

# Decompose the `src/commands/doctor.ts` god class

**File:** `src/commands/doctor.ts` (1,658 lines at intake time; 1,582 when the item was created)

## Problem statement

`src/commands/doctor.ts` is a single 1,658-line module that carries the entire
`wl doctor` CLI surface: six module-level notice/formatting helpers at the top
and eleven command registrations (root `doctor` validation, `upgrade`,
`stage-sync`, `prune`, `cache`, `foreign-items`, `audit-gaps`,
`dangling-parents`, `priority`, `file-paths`, `migrate`), each with its own
inline `async` action body. The `--fix` interactive flow and the findings
aggregation of the root command alone occupy ~385 lines inside one nested
callback. Navigating, reviewing or changing one subcommand requires holding the
other ten in view, so every doctor change carries avoidable regression risk and
the file sits above the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7.

## Users

- **CLI maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one doctor subcommand
  (e.g. `prune`, `file-paths`, the `--fix` prompt) without reasoning about
  1,600 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need a diff attributable to a single subcommand so the
  blast radius of a change is legible.
- **Future agents implementing doctor work items** (e.g. the open
  WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J `wl doctor prefix` item) need a named, findable module
  per subcommand instead of appending to a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent adding a new doctor subcommand, I want an existing per-subcommand
  module template so that registration is mechanical and reviewable.
- As a reviewer, I want a `prune` change to touch only the prune module and its
  tests so that I can verify it against its own suite.
- As a maintainer, I want every doctor file under 1,000 lines so that it is
  readable in a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for
   `src/commands/doctor.ts` (now a thin registrar) and for every module created
   by the split.
2. **Public entry point unchanged.** `src/commands/doctor.ts` still provides
   `export default function register(ctx: PluginContext): void`, so
   `src/command-registry.ts` (`doctor: () => import('./commands/doctor.js')`)
   and every existing CLI test import path keep working with **no importer
   edits**.
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No change to subcommand names,
   flags, help text, human output strings, JSON payload shapes or exit codes; no
   existing test file is modified (import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all existing `doctor` CLI/integration tests (`tests/cli/doctor-*.test.ts`,
   `tests/doctor-*.test.ts`) pass unmodified.
4. **One concern per module.** Each extracted module registers exactly one
   doctor subcommand — or, for the shared notices module, one cohesive
   cross-cutting concern — carries a module-level doc comment stating its single
   responsibility, and moves its provenance comments (work-item ids) with the
   code.
5. **No cycles, narrow seams.** Extracted modules never import from
   `src/commands/doctor.ts`; the registrar passes a narrow typed context
   (`program`/`output`/`utils` and `dataPath` only where needed) so handlers do
   not depend on the full `PluginContext` surface.
6. **Line-count guard test (additive).** A new test asserts the doctor module
   family stays at or under 1,000 lines per file and fails when any module
   exceeds the ceiling (mirrors the `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`
   precedent from WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E — no existing test is touched).
7. **Documentation updated.** Any repository notes that describe the doctor
   command layout (e.g. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLI.md`, `docs/migrations.md`
   references) remain accurate, and the new module layout is stated in the
   top-of-file doc comment of `src/commands/doctor.ts`.
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate the existing action bodies and helpers into sibling
  modules, adjust imports and registration wiring; do not refactor their logic,
  rename flags, or reword user-facing output.
- **Entry point is fixed.** `src/commands/doctor.ts` must remain the dynamic
  import target in `src/command-registry.ts`; the split happens *behind* that
  path.
- **CLI-agnostic logic stays put.** `src/doctor/*.ts` holds CLI-independent
  validation logic (`status-stage-check`, `dependency-check`, `file-paths-check`,
  `hook-upgrade`, `foreign-items-check`, `audit-gaps-check`, `parent-check`,
  `podcast-scripts-check`, `fix`). It is consumed as-is; this item does not
  restructure it.
- **Serial, tree-green landing.** Extract the smallest subcommands first and the
  root validation/`--fix` action last, so every intermediate state builds and
  passes the suite.
- **No new runtime dependencies.** No changes to the doctor CLI contract, and no
  edits to the TUI or other commands.

## Existing state

`src/commands/doctor.ts` is 1,658 lines on today's `dev`. Inventory of logical
sections (line ranges from the current checkout):

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | File header + imports | 1–30 | 30 |
| 2 | `DAY_MS` constant | 31 | 1 |
| 3 | `formatCacheBytes` helper | 33–46 | 14 |
| 4 | `DoctorOptions` type | 47–50 | 4 |
| 5 | `PendingUpgradeState` + `detectPendingUpgrades` | 51–92 | 42 |
| 6 | `buildPendingUpgradeFinding` | 93–129 | 37 |
| 7 | `printPendingUpgradeNotice` | 130–151 | 22 |
| 8 | `PendingCacheState` + `detectPendingCacheState` | 152–196 | 45 |
| 9 | `printPendingCacheNotice` | 197–207 | 11 |
| 10 | `register()` prologue + root `doctor` command definition | 208–217 | 10 |
| 11 | `doctor upgrade` action | 218–418 | 201 |
| 12 | `doctor stage-sync` action | 420–549 | 130 |
| 13 | `doctor prune` action | 551–649 | 99 |
| 14 | `doctor cache` action | 651–715 | 65 |
| 15 | `doctor foreign-items` action | 717–838 | 122 |
| 16 | `doctor audit-gaps` action | 840–877 | 38 |
| 17 | `doctor dangling-parents` action | 879–948 | 70 |
| 18 | `doctor priority` action | 950–1036 | 87 |
| 19 | `doctor file-paths` action | 1038–1150 | 113 |
| 20 | `doctor migrate` action | 1152–1271 | 120 |
| 21 | Root `doctor` action (findings aggregation, `--fix` interactive prompt, notices) | 1273–1657 | 385 |

Relevant structural facts discovered during intake:

- **Single consumer.** Only `src/command-registry.ts` imports the module
  (`doctor: () => import('./commands/doctor.js')`), and only for the default
  export. There is no cross-module use of helpers defined in the file, so
  extraction needs no public barrel beyond the unchanged default export.
- **Existing precedent for a nested sibling directory.** `src/sync.ts` (1,828
  lines, itself the subject of WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ) already sits beside a
  `src/sync/` directory (`src/sync/merge-utils.ts`), so `src/commands/doctor.ts`
  + `src/commands/doctor/` follows an established repository shape.
- **CLI layer vs validation layer.** `src/doctor/` modules are pure,
  `PluginContext`-free validators; the monolith's bulk is CLI registration and
  output rendering. The split therefore belongs in the command layer, not in
  `src/doctor/`.
- **Test surface to keep green (unmodified).** 18 existing doctor suites —
  `tests/doctor-{dependency-check,file-paths,foreign-items-apply,foreign-items-check,hook-upgrade,podcast-scripts,retired-stage,status-stage}.test.ts`
  and `tests/cli/doctor-{audit-gaps,cache,foreign-items-apply,foreign-items-push,foreign-items,priority,prune,stage-sync,upgrade-notice,upgrade}.test.ts`.
  Source: `ls tests/doctor-*.test.ts tests/cli/doctor-*.test.ts`.

## Desired change

Reduce `src/commands/doctor.ts` to a thin registrar that wires the root
`doctor` command and delegates each subcommand to its own module under a new
`src/commands/doctor/` directory. Starting decomposition (boundaries are an
implementation decision, subject to the constraints above):

| New module | Responsibility | Approx. size |
|---|---|---|

# Remove dead top-level `singleFork` key in vitest.config.ts

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

`vitest.config.ts` sets `singleFork: true` at the top level of the `test`
block. Vitest 4 has no such top-level option — `singleFork` is a
`poolOptions.forks.*` key — so the setting is silently ignored (no warning is
emitted). The comment directly above it, "Force per-file isolation by limiting
to 1 active worker per file sequence", describes behaviour that is actually
provided by `isolate: true` + `maxWorkers: 4` (+ `pool: 'forks'`).

The dead key is harmless today, but it is misleading: a future reader may
believe the suite is serialised, and a migration to an option shape that *is*
read (or vitest version churn that starts warning) could confuse diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `singleFork: true` is removed from `vitest.config.ts`.
- The comment above it is rewritten (or removed) to state what actually
  enforces per-file isolation (`pool: 'forks'`, `isolate: true`,
  `maxWorkers: 4`), and that parallelism is otherwise intentional.
- Full canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) stays green with the same
  test counts; no runtime regression in either wall-clock or aggregate test
  time on the same host.

## Out of scope

Bumping `maxWorkers` / `fileParallelism` — that is the follow-up "Test-suite
parallelism: reconsider maxWorkers on hosts with more cores".

# Investigate in-process CLI harness cost (~200 ms per invocation)

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

Timing the in-process CLI harness (`tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts`,
`runInProcess()`, used by `execAsync` in `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`):

- `--help` (no DB work): ~72 ms per invocation
- `list --json`, `create`, `status`: ~196–257 ms per invocation

The canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) makes roughly 1200 such
in-process invocations — about 240 s of aggregate test time across
`close-recursive` (46 tests), `issue-management` (49), `issue-status` (43),
`valid-json-output` (38) and `json-output-shape` (18), plus seeding in
`beforeEach` hooks.

Every invocation constructs a fresh `Command`, re-registers ~35 built-in
commands, loads config, opens a SQLite database (with schema/migrations) and
closes it. The suite measured 624 s → 427–547 s after WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8, and
this in-process pool is the next largest remaining aggregate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Profile one `runInProcess` call and attribute the per-call cost
  (commander registration vs config load vs DB open/close vs command action).
- Where the cost is test-harness overhead (not production behaviour being
  asserted), reduce it without changing what each test asserts — candidates:
  reusing the command/plugin-context across calls for stateless reads,
  avoiding repeated YAML config parses, sharing DB open across calls within a
  test file.
- If the cost is production CLI startup (DB schema/migrations, plugin scan),
  record the findings and re-scope: the change then belongs in `src/` and is a
  production decision, not a test-only change.
- Canonical suite stays green with unchanged test counts; median wall-clock
  on a consistent host improves versus the pre-change baseline of this item.

# Test-suite parallelism: reconsider maxWorkers on hosts with more cores

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

The canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) runs with `maxWorkers: 4`
in `vitest.config.ts` (pool `'forks'`, `isolate: true`). The dev host has 16
cores. WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 reduced per-spawn cost ~5× (bundle-based CLI
spawning) and cut the wall clock 30–35 % at matched load, but wall clock
remains dominated by the longest single files on the critical path
(`sync-vs-mutation` ~151 s, `close-recursive` ~121 s, `issue-management`
~88 s, `read-cache-spawn-reduction` ~84 s).

The brief explicitly listed parallelisation as out of scope ("record as
linked follow-up work items, not this brief") — hence this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Measure the canonical suite at `maxWorkers` 4 vs 6 vs 8 on a 16-core host
  (median of ≥3 runs per setting, load quoted per run; report aggregate test
  time as the load-independent metric).
- Confirm memory headroom: RSS per worker tracked; no OOM at the chosen
  setting (the config comment cites memory guardrails as the reason for 4).
- Confirm determinism: 3 consecutive green runs at the chosen setting, no
  intermittent test-timeout or hook-timeout failures.
- Decide and record: either adopt a higher `maxWorkers` (documented) or
  formally keep 4 with the measurement evidence.

The skill (scripts/metrics.py) classifies process_count/thread_count as critical (warn: 32, crit: 64) using single-user calibrated thresholds. A herdr multi-agent host with 16-21 concurrent pi sessions legitimately runs 560-580 processes / 2250+ threads at all times, so the metric is permanently red. Thread count and swap_usage warning values also need recalibration. Suggest: derive thresholds from core count / session count (e.g. warn = cores*4, crit = cores*8) or make per-host config overridable in config.yaml. discovered-from:machine-hygiene-session-2025-10-21

# Maintenance routines skill: create/maintain daily scheduled test, standup, refactor sessions at high priority

## Headline

A new ContextHub skill (`/skill:maintenance-routines`) that creates and maintains the required daily scheduled maintenance sessions (test 07:00, standup 08:00, refactor 09:00) in each project's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatching all of them at **high request priority** so they are processed even in peak periods — backed by a herdr enhancement that threads a per-entry `priority` (default `high`) into the `X-Priority` request header.

## Problem statement

Every project should run regular automated maintenance routines (test suite, standup report, refactor pass). The herdr plugin already has the mechanism (`scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatched on idle by the downtime worker), but there is no maintained, canonical set: the current template/live config only carries `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (06:05, no priority), and **no** `/skill:test` routine. Worse, dispatched scheduled prompts have no work item, so they receive the downtime request-priority default `medium` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium`) — they can be starved behind peak-period contention. The operator wants the three routines scheduled daily (07:00/08:00/09:00) and dispatched at **high** priority.

## Users

- **Project operator** — wants the three routines to reliably exist in each project's schedule and to be processed even in peak periods.
- **Automated maintenance sessions** (`/skill:test`, `/skill:standup`, `/skill:refactor`) — must carry `X-Priority: high` on every provider request so `llama-proxy` serves them ahead of the contention queue.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I run `/skill:maintenance-routines` on a project and it ensures `/skill:test` (daily 07:00), `/skill:standup` (daily 08:00) and `/skill:refactor` (daily 09:00) are present and correctly configured in `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, without touching my last-run timestamps or any custom entries.
- As an operator, I know every scheduled maintenance session is dispatched with `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY=high` (→ `X-Priority: high`), so the daily test/standup/refactor runs are served even during peak periods.
- As an operator, when I provision a new project with `wl init`, it comes pre-loaded with the same three routines (daily, timed, high priority).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Skill exists and reconciles the schedule.** `skill/maintenance-routines/` ships a `SKILL.md`, a reconciler script and unit tests. Invoking it (or the script directly) reconciles the project-local `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (under the resolved worklog dir) so these required routines are present and exact:
   - `/skill:test` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "07:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:standup` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "08:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:refactor` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "09:00"`, `priority: "high"`
2. **Reconcile is non-destructive and idempotent.** Entries are created if absent; drifted fields (interval/time/priority) are corrected; `lastTriggeredAt` and all other user-defined entries are preserved verbatim; a second run makes no further changes; missing or malformed config files are handled fail-closed with a clear report; `--dry-run` shows the planned diff without writing.
3. **Herdr honours a per-entry `priority` field.** `ScheduledPrompt` gains an optional `priority` (`low|medium|high|critical`) validated in `parseScheduledPrompt` (invalid value → entry skipped with a warning, fail-closed); **absent → defaults to `high`** for scheduled prompts. The scheduled-prompt dispatch passes it through `spawnAgentPane({ priority })` → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (so `high` → `X-Priority: high` on every request). Unit tests cover parse defaults/validation and the dispatch threading.
4. **Template provisions the required set.** `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the `wl init` base set) is updated to the three required routines with daily `intervalDays`, `time` and `priority: high`, so new projects are provisioned with the routines (create-if-absent semantics unchanged — existing configs are never clobbered).
5. **Documentation criterion.** `packages/herdr/README.md` (Scheduled prompts section), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (Request priority section) and `CONFIG.md` (Scheduled-prompts config section) document the new `priority` field, the default-`high` behaviour, and the three routines; the maintenance-routines skill is referenced from the relevant skill docs listing.
6. **Testing criterion.** Skill tests (`pytest` under `skill/maintenance-routines/tests/`) cover reconcile/idempotence/preservation/dry-run; herdr unit tests (`vitest`) cover the new parse/validation and dispatch priority; full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No changes to the interactive dispatch path or to the other downtime tiers' mapping tables** (`request-priority.ts` stays fixed); only the scheduled-prompt entry schema, its dispatch call, and the skill/template change.
- The requested **default is `high`** for scheduled prompts (operator decision Q1): an entry that wants lower priority must set the field explicitly (`low`/`medium`). This is a deliberate change from the current downtime default (`medium`) for scheduled prompts only.
- No code-behaviour changes to `wl init` — only the **contents** of `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the provisioning path and create-if-absent semantics stay as-is).
- The skill must be safe to run from any project root (`wl`-independent — it reads/writes only `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, atomic tmp+rename, matching herdr's `saveScheduledPrompts` pattern).

## Existing state

- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (and the live `/.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`) currently carry only `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (daily `time: "06:05"`); no `/skill:test`; no priority field anywhere.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — schema (`id|prompt|intervalDays|lastTriggeredAt|time?`), fail-closed parse, due-check, atomic persist; **no priority support**.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchScheduledPrompt` calls `spawnAgentPane(prompt.prompt, { model, cwd, paneName, anchorId })` with **no priority** → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions({ priority: undefined })` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium` (docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md, "Scheduled prompts have no work item and get the downtime default (medium)").
- `src/commands/init.ts` — `ensureScheduledPromptsInstalled` copies the template create-if-absent; unchanged in behaviour.
- Skills precedent: `skill/heartbeat/` and `skill/pane-triage/` (SKILL.md + scripts + tests, tracked in ContextHub, deployed to `~/.pi/agent/skills/<name>`); shared helpers in `skill/shared/`.

## Desired change

1. **New skill** `skill/maintenance-routines/`: `SKILL.md` (spec: required-routines table, invocation, admission of a bootstrap `/skill:maintenance-routines` schedule), `scripts/maintenance_routines.py` (reconcile + `--dry-run`; atomic writes; preserves `lastTriggeredAt` and foreign entries), `tests/` (unit tests).
2. **Herdr priority support**: extend `ScheduledPrompt` + `parseScheduledPrompt` with optional `priority` (default `high`); thread it from `dispatchScheduledPrompt` → `spawnAgentPane({ priority })` → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`. `mapDowntimeRequestPriority` already maps `high`→`high`.
3. **Template**: update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` to the three routines (daily, timed, `priority: "high"`).
4. **Docs**: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CONFIG.md`; skill listed alongside heartbeat/pane-triage where appropriate.
5. **Tests**: pytest for the skill reconciler; vitest for parse/validation + dispatch threading in herdr.

## Key Files

- `skill/maintenance-routines/SKILL.md` — new skill spec (required-routines table, usage, dry-run).
- `skill/maintenance-routines/scripts/maintenance_routines.py` — new reconciler CLI (`--dry-run`, atomic write, preserves state).
- `skill/maintenance-routines/tests/test_maintenance_routines.py` — new unit tests (reconcile, idempotence, preservation, malformed config, dry-run).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — add optional `priority` (`low|medium|high|critical`, default `high`), validation in `parseScheduledPrompt`.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.test.ts` — new parse/default/validation cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchScheduledPrompt` passes `prompt.priority` to `spawnAgentPane`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (or the scheduled-prompts tier test) — dispatch threads `priority: 'high'` into the spawn opts/env.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` — updated to the three required routines.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CONFIG.md` — document the new field/default and the routines.
- `tests/skill/maintenance-routines/` — integration-style tests for the skill (repo test-suite convention, cf. `tests/skill/heartbeat/`).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX** (completed) — herdr downtime dispatcher: scheduled prompts (best-effort frequency) config — the mechanism the skill maintains.
- **WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH / WL-0MVF3Q3VL000UNCN** (completed) — request priority (`X-Priority`) mapping tables and `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` env threading — the priority plumbing we reuse.
- **WL-0MTF5UAJ4000LLZ9** (completed) — removal of scheduled-prompts console output (no-op here).
- **WL-0MUKYERLZ006ELL5** (completed) — non-terminal cooldown for dispatched panes (context for scheduled dispatch behaviour).
- **WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B** (completed) — periodic request scheduling to the pi worklog plugin; the scheduled-prompts feature parent.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B** – Add periodic request scheduling to pi worklog plugin (completed)
- **WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR** – Scheduled prompts: add time-of-day dispatch (time window) to scheduled-prompts tier (completed)
- **WL-0MKRPG64S04PL1A6** – wl doctor (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: convey, create, creates, currently, daily (+26 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: create, creates, daily, default, dispatched (+25 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: convey, create, creates, currently, default (+23 more)
- Skill-authoring precedents: `skill/heartbeat/`, `skill/pane-triage/` (SKILL.md + scripts + tests, deployed to `~/.pi/agent/skills`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — default-`high` changes politeness of ALL scheduled prompts** (including custom future entries). Accepted by operator (Q1: "default high"); any entry can opt down via an explicit `low`/`medium` field. Mitigation: document prominently.
- **Risk — parse strictness.** An invalid `priority` value rejects the whole entry (consistent with existing `time` handling) — a config typo could silently disable a routine. Mitigation: the skill always writes a valid value; tests cover the failure path.
- **Risk — skill/template drift.** If `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` is later edited, the skill's required table may diverge. Mitigation: keep the required-routines table in one place (the skill), and the template mirrors it (as Q3).
- **Assumption — the skill runs per project root.** Invoked via a pi session (herdr pane or manual) with `cwd` at the project root; it reads/writes only `<cwd>/.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (worklog-dir safe).
- **Assumption — operators may bootstrap the skill itself as a scheduled prompt** (e.g. daily `/skill:maintenance-routines`) to keep the schedule self-healing; not required for this item.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no changes to interactive dispatch, `request-priority.ts` tables, other downtime tiers, or `wl init` code; any opportunity discovered during implementation is recorded as a new linked work item, not added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: How should scheduled routines get high priority?**
  - Options: (a) per-entry `priority` field in `scheduled-prompts.json`, threaded through herdr dispatch → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`; (b) herdr always dispatches all scheduled prompts at `high`; (c) config-level default priority.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): "1. A (default high)"** — per-entry field; **absent → default `high`**.
  - Reasoning recorded: matches "all those work items should be sent high priority so they get processed even in peak periods"; keeps intent in the config; future entries can opt down explicitly.
- **Q2: How strictly should the skill maintain the required set?**
  - Options: (a) ensure the three required routines exist & match spec (create-if-absent, fix drifted fields), keep other user entries; (b) strict whitelist (remove anything else); (c) create-if-absent only (never fix drift).
  - **Answer (producer): "2. A"** — non-destructive reconcile, preserve custom entries.
- **Q3: Should new projects get the routines by default?**
  - Options: (a) also update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the `wl init` base set); (b) skill-only.
  - **Answer (producer): "3. A"** — template updated so every new project provisions the three routines at 07:00/08:00/09:00 high (`wl init` code path unchanged).

## Problem

The downtime dispatcher's no-dispatch decision log (`<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`) is capped at **100 lines** (rolling). On a busy machine that is roughly **one hour** of history, because every tick that is refused for a capacity/prefill reason writes a decision entry.

During the 2026-10-22/23 overnight starvation investigation this meant the whole night could not be reconstructed: the retained window started at `2026-10-23T05:59:58Z` and the decisions for the preceding ~8 hours had already been rotated out. The pre-05:30 reasons had to be *inferred* from pi session activity instead of read from the log.

For contrast, the retained 84-minute window carried 66 no-dispatch decisions — so the cap is genuinely exhausted in about an hour of saturated polling.

## Why it matters

- Capacity-saturation starvation is silent by design (NOP), so the decision log is the **only** forensic evidence that dispatch was attempted and why it was refused.
- Post-mortem of an overnight outage ("why did almost nothing dispatch?") is currently impossible after the fact; the operator has to guess.
- The same problem affects distinguishing `capacity-saturated` / `slots-unavailable` / `prefill-cap` / `idle-age-pending` / `no-candidate` / `review-queue-hold` / `code-freeze` after rotation.

## Goal

As an operator, I want at least a full night (24 h) of downtime dispatch decisions to remain available on a busy machine, so that a post-mortem can report the actual terminal reasons and their counts, with bounded disk use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — On a machine producing decision entries at the observed rate (≥ 60/hour), at least the **last 24 hours** of `no-dispatch` decisions are readable after the fact (verified by a test that writes > 1,500 entries and asserts the oldest 24 h window is still present).
- [ ] AC2 — Disk growth is bounded: rotation happens on a documented size/time policy (e.g. daily files with a retention window, or size-based rotation with N kept), and the policy is configurable with a documented default.
- [ ] AC3 — An operator-facing, documented way exists to reconstruct a time-range summary (e.g. `wl`/herdr command, or documented `grep`/`jq` recipe over rotated files) that prints a reason tally per hour for a given night.
- [ ] AC4 — Existing readers/parsers of the single `downtime-coordination.log` path are either migrated atomically or continue to read the newest file without change; no dispatch decision is lost across a rotation boundary (test asserted).
- [ ] AC5 — Docs updated: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` log-schema/observability section names the retention policy and the summary recipe.

## Evidence (2026-10-23 investigation)

- `ContextHub/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`: 100 entries covering `2026-10-23T05:59:58.509Z` → `2026-10-23T07:13:27.061Z`.
- Reason tally in that retained window: `capacity-saturated` 29, `slots-unavailable` 29, `idle-age-pending` 4, `prefill-cap` 2, `idle-age-qualified` 2 (66 no-dispatch decisions).
- Earlier overnight window (roughly `2026-10-22T21:00Z` → `2026-10-23T05:30Z`) had no retained decision records at all.

## Notes

- Related: the starvation investigation item covering long-running panes holding local-LLM capacity.
- No production behaviour change to dispatch decisions is in scope — this is observability only.
